title: Next-Generation Operation
content: **nextGeneration A**: Produces all values $xy - 1$ for distinct $x, y \in A$ with $xy \geq 2$. Formalized as the set $\{z : \mathbb{N} \mid \exists x\, y,\; x \in A \wedge y \in A \wedge x \neq y \wedge xy \geq 2 \wedge z = xy - 1\}$. The condition $xy \geq 2$ ensures the subtraction stays in $\mathbb{N}$ (avoiding underflow). This is the fundamental building block: applying it iteratively from the seed $\{2, 3\}$ generates the entire sequence.
mathContext: $\text{nextGeneration}(A) = \{xy - 1 : x, y \in A,\; x \neq y,\; xy \geq 2\}$

title: Iterated Sequence of Sets
content: **sequenceSet n**: The $n$-th generation of the iterative construction. Defined by $S_0 = \{2, 3\}$ and $S_{n+1} = S_n \cup \text{nextGeneration}(S_n)$. Each generation accumulates all new products-minus-one from elements already present. The sequence is monotone increasing: $S_0 \subseteq S_1 \subseteq S_2 \subseteq \cdots$.
mathContext: $S_0 = \{2, 3\},\quad S_{n+1} = S_n \cup \{xy - 1 : x, y \in S_n,\; x \neq y\}$

title: Full Generated Set
content: **generatedSet**: The union $S = \bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} S_n$ of all generations. This is the complete set of integers eventually produced by the iterative process. An integer $m$ belongs to $S$ iff it appears in some finite generation $S_n$. The density of this set is the central object of study in Problem #424.

title: Counting Function
content: **generatedCount N**: The number of elements of `generatedSet` in $\{1, \ldots, N\}$, computed as $|\text{Finset.Icc}(1, N).\text{filter}(\lambda n.\, n \in S)|$. This is the numerator in the density ratio $|S \cap [1,N]|/N$. Marked `noncomputable` because membership in `generatedSet` (a countable union) is not decidable.

title: Erdos Problem #424: Positive Density Conjecture
content: **erdos_424_conjecture**: Axiomatizes the positive lower density conjecture: $\exists c > 0, \forall N > 0, |S \cap [1,N]| \geq cN$. This is the main open question—does the generated set contain a positive proportion of all natural numbers? The formulation uses a uniform lower bound $cN$ rather than a liminf, which is a slightly stronger statement but equivalent for monotone counting functions.

title: Mod 3 Obstruction
content: **mod_3_obstruction**: Axiomatizes that no element of the generated set is congruent to 1 modulo 3: $\forall n \in S,\; n \bmod 3 \neq 1$. The proof is by induction on generations: the seeds $2 \equiv 2$ and $3 \equiv 0$ are not $\equiv 1 \pmod{3}$, and if $a, b \not\equiv 1 \pmod{3}$ then $ab \bmod 3 \in \{0 \cdot 0, 0 \cdot 2, 2 \cdot 0, 2 \cdot 2\} = \{0, 0, 0, 1\} \pmod{3}$, so $ab - 1 \bmod 3 \in \{2, 2, 2, 0\}$, never 1. This eliminates one-third of all integers from the set.

title: Density Upper Bound 2/3
content: **density_upper_bound**: Axiomatizes that the density of the generated set is at most $2/3 + \varepsilon$ for any $\varepsilon > 0$ and sufficiently large $N$: $\forall \varepsilon > 0, \exists N_0, \forall N \geq N_0, |S \cap [1,N]| \leq (2/3 + \varepsilon)N$. This follows directly from the mod 3 obstruction: since one residue class is entirely excluded, at most $2/3$ of integers can appear. The $\varepsilon$-formulation captures the asymptotic nature of the bound.

title: Initial Elements of the Sequence
content: **initial_elements**: Axiomatizes that the first six elements $2, 3, 5, 9, 14, 17$ belong to `generatedSet`. These are computed: $2 \cdot 3 - 1 = 5$, $2 \cdot 5 - 1 = 9$, $3 \cdot 5 - 1 = 14$, $2 \cdot 9 - 1 = 17$. The sequence continues $26, 44, 69, \ldots$ (OEIS A005244). Verifying membership provides a sanity check on the definitions.

title: Monotonicity of Generations
content: **sequence_monotone**: Axiomatizes that $S_n \subseteq S_{n+1}$ for all $n$. This follows immediately from the definition $S_{n+1} = S_n \cup \text{nextGeneration}(S_n)$, since $S_n \subseteq S_n \cup X$ for any $X$. Monotonicity ensures that the generated set is well-defined as a union and that elements, once added, are never removed.

title: Closure Under the Operation
content: **generated_closed**: Axiomatizes that `generatedSet` is closed under $(x, y) \mapsto xy - 1$ for distinct $x, y$ with $xy \geq 2$: if $x, y \in S$ with $x \neq y$ and $xy \geq 2$, then $xy - 1 \in S$. This is the fixed-point characterization of the generated set—it is the smallest set containing $\{2, 3\}$ that is closed under this operation. Equivalently, $S$ is the closure of $\{2, 3\}$ under the binary operation.
mathContext: $x, y \in S,\; x \neq y,\; xy \geq 2 \Rightarrow xy - 1 \in S$
